note: Cases CLAUDE.md invariant 7 and registry-oracle-notes.md §11 name as the known ways to be confidently wrong, plus the requiredness pass's (maintenance/probes/requiredness/). Each defeated some plausible parser. `expect_null_validated` / `expect_strict_null` are the two sets the old single `expect_required` conflated. `occurrence` picks the Nth `CODEC` field in a file with nested codecs; `inline` cases are synthetic sources for shapes with no real instance. The last two real cases assert STRUCTURE (were the keys found at all) rather than copying the parser's output: their key counts come from counting `new KeyedCodec` in the file independently.

cases.label: raw KeyedCodec + true THIRD ARGUMENT = strict_null, NOT required
cases.why: `new KeyedCodec("Shapes", new MapCodec<...>(...), true)` - raw, so a pattern expecting KeyedCodec<T> skips it and undercounts; and strict_null by the third argument, so stopping at the first balanced paren keeps the key but loses the flag. Its four keys include exactly one strict_null and NONE null_validated: deleting `Shapes` from a shipped asset still decodes, measured live (maintenance/probes/requiredness/run.sh, R1 rows).

cases.label: raw KeyedCodec + true INSIDE the inner constructor = not strict_null
cases.why: Same key NAME `Shapes`, also raw, but `new KeyedCodec("Shapes", new SetCodec<...>(..., true))` - two arguments, the true inside the inner constructor. Attributing it to the outer codec manufactures strict_null on a key that has none. The key that IS strict_null here is `IncludeOrExclude` (a genuine third argument), so the pair discriminates by which paren the `true` sits in.

cases.label: null_validated by Validators.nonNull() attached AFTER append(...) closes
cases.why: `Name` is the sole key carrying Validators.nonNull() (PluginManifest.java:53), so it is the only key whose omission fails decode. Parsing to the first balanced paren reports NO null_validated keys at all, because the validator attaches on the builder two calls further along, before .add(). No key is strict_null.

cases.label: same simple name, different file, different key and requiredness
cases.why: The twin of the `StartObjective` interaction in the 44. Both declare exactly ONE key, so a count cross-check agrees while the key name and its requiredness are both wrong: this one is `ObjectiveId`, validated by nothing; the registered interaction is `Setup`, null_validated.

cases.label: chain on a *_BUILDER field, .build()-ed into the public codec
cases.why: Item.CODEC is `CODEC_BUILDER.build()`. Scanning the CODEC statement alone returns ZERO keys and the appends==adds==keys self-check ENDORSES it — on the corpus's most-documented asset type (items.md plus five items-*.md pages). One key, `State`, is appended to the builder ~700 lines BELOW the declaration, so following the field is necessary but not sufficient; the scan must also collect appends on that field elsewhere in the file.
cases.expect_keys_note: 0.7.2: 60, counted independently as `new KeyedCodec` occurrences in Item.java (59 at 0.6.8); the new key is `Ability`.

cases.label: .addField(...) declares keys too
cases.why: Matching only .append/.appendInherited misses .addField — 273 uses across 41 classes in build-26. This class declares all 8 of its keys that way and parsed as zero with the self-check green.

cases.label: BuilderCodec.abstractBuilder puts the PARENT in argument ONE
cases.why: `BuilderCodec.builder(X.class, X::new, Parent.CODEC)` puts the parent third; `BuilderCodec.abstractBuilder(X.class, Parent.CODEC)` puts it SECOND, and a parser reading args[2] records no parent at all. 96 chains in build-26 use abstractBuilder against 1516 plain builders, so it looks negligible and is not: every one of them is a BASE class, which is precisely what other chains inherit from. Found by auditing why 15 inherited-scope bindings were rejected on `Next` — a key SimpleInteraction declares and the walk could not reach, because the link was severed at the first abstract base.

cases.label: nonEmptyArray() is a NonNullValidator subclass: the literal `nonNull()` text misses it
cases.why: RunOnBlockTypesInteraction.java:63 attaches Validators.nonEmptyArray() to BlockSets, and NonEmptyArrayValidator extends NonNullValidator, so BuilderField.nonNullValidator is set and an omitted BlockSets fails decode (probe config `e`). The parser matched only the literal `Validators.nonNull()`, so it called this key unvalidated - 21 keys at 0.7.2 were missed that way. All four keys are strict_null (flag at :55/:59/:63/:67), which makes none of them required: the old union listed all four.

cases.label: nonEmptyArray() alone, then an .addField() key after it
cases.why: AnimationSet.CODEC (ModelAsset.java:400-404): `Animations` carries only nonEmptyArray() and no nonNull(); `NextAnimationDelay` is an .addField() with no validator. The old tail scan, bracket-aware but not call-aware, ran past an addField (no `.add()` terminates it) into the next append's validators.

cases.label: .addField() keys do not inherit the next append's validators
cases.why: Animation.CODEC (ModelAsset.java:446-451): `Looping` and `Weight` are .addField() keys followed by an .append() whose validator chain is later; the old parser credited both with it (they showed as validator-required). Only `Animation` carries nonNull() here.

cases.label: RecordCodec: the validator is INSIDE the append group, not after it
cases.why: RecordCodec.builder(..).append(new KeyedCodec("Message", Message.CODEC, true), accessor, opts -> opts.documentation(..).addValidator(Validators.nonNull())). There is no `.add()`, so the tail scan that works for BuilderCodec never sees the validator; the old parser called this key validator-less and, worse, let a record's earlier keys swallow later keys' validators (WorldEventRecord.Id was shown validator-required). Probe rows rS-b/rS-c: omission of such a key fails decode.

inline.label: inline: subclass-only, explicit INSTANCE, composite and element validators
inline: addField followed by an append that has nonNull
inline: RecordCodec with lambda, direct and absent validators
inline.src: public static final RecordCodec<R> CODEC = RecordCodec.builder(R.class).append(new KeyedCodec("Lam", Codec.STRING, true), R::a, opts -> opts.documentation("d").addValidator(Validators.nonNull())).append(new KeyedCodec("None", Codec.STRING, false), R::b).append(new KeyedCodec("Direct", Codec.STRING), R::c, Validators.nonNull()).append(new KeyedCodec("Doc", Codec.STRING), R::d, opts -> opts.documentation("only")).build(R::new);
